title: test-0135-GEN-VOTING
passage: In India, every citizen who is 18 years of age or older has the right to vote, regardless of their education or property ownership. To ensure fairness, the Election Commission operates as an independent body, separate from the control of the ruling government. Before an election, the Model Code of Conduct comes into effect to guide the behavior of political parties and candidates, though it is a set of guidelines rather than a strict criminal law. When you go to vote, you use an Electronic Voting Machine (EVM), which is a standalone device not connected to any internet or Wi-Fi network. After you press the button for your chosen candidate, a VVPAT machine prints a slip that you can see through a glass window for seven seconds, but this slip stays inside the machine and cannot be taken home. If you do not wish to support any candidate, you can select the NOTA option on the EVM. Selecting NOTA is a formal way to express your choice, and it is counted as a valid vote, even though it does not cancel the election if it receives the most votes. Voting is a voluntary right in our democracy, meaning you are free to choose whether or not to participate without facing any government punishment.
